review.head: f9f82a146fb0
review.note: Code change confined to validate.ts (a-truth.gate.test.ts untouched; only generated projections alongside). Gate at test/gates/a-truth.gate.test.ts:75 now discriminates: pre-fix 'send x to mailbox home' on W4 (worlds/W4.json: authority prompt.send@1=consent-required, sole realization d1-virtual.prompt.send@1 serves provider:claude only) returned needs-consent, which is outside the allowed set, so the gate was red; validate.ts:121-129 adds the provider-serving check returning unavailable. Evidence file shows exactly one flip (fail->pass) and pass 39->40 with REGRESSED 0. No side effects: the loop only reads, mirrors the existing decl.params.find(...)! pattern at validate.ts:79, and the !account continue is unreachable-as-a-hole because heldBy already routed unknown ids to needs-info. Compatible targets unaffected (verified: W4 claude-work -> needs-consent / ready / refused under consent-required/allowed/denied). Ordering: the new check sits after the pre-existing capability-level realization check and before authority, so incompatible -> unavailable under all three authority states; this is the established convention, not a new inversion, but it means denied+incompatible now reports unavailable rather than refused -- an inherited-ordering observation for the ordering owner. Two scope notes, neither a defect in this commit: (1) this commit added no tests -- 2 of the 3 promoted D1-006 gates were already green from bc226dc, so D1-006 must not be read later as 'three new tests written'; the locked gate is also a permissive negative (allows unavailable/needs-choice/unknown/refused) rather than asserting unavailable plus its reason. (2) The fix is provider-only and ignores freshness, while the module's canonical compatibleAccounts (src/world.ts:92-95) also requires freshness==='fresh': on W3 the stale account yields compatibleAccounts=[] yet validateInterpretation returns needs-consent, and ready under authority=allowed. That is pre-existing, not introduced here, and belongs to D1-016/D1-017, not to D1-006's closure.

review.head: ee1be8a11d71
review.note: ACCEPT (independent, adversarial). Verified at HEAD 76fe02b, working tree clean for the reviewed files. Gate hardening is real: both original D1-016 assertions are retained verbatim and four gates now run under a forced authority=allowed World (b-world.gate.test.ts:72-86), so the verdict is decided by freshness rather than by needs-consent. Discrimination proven by mutation, not by reading: deleting the single freshness line (validate.ts:130) from a /tmp copy turns EXACTLY one gate red - 'W3 stale Account is refused for freshness even when authority allows it' - while the pre-existing 'W3 stale Account can never yield a READY command' stays green, which is the direct confirmation of dev-trv-1110's finding that the original gate was vacuous. Positive control is one-factor: with the authority map merged identically in both arms, W3-stale -> needs-info ('account: \account:claude-work\ is stale, not fresh') and W3-fresh -> ready. The blocker is load-bearing end to end, not just a label: dispatch commit is rejected NOT_READY needs-info for the stale Account and granted only for the fresh control; granting consent does not revive it. Freshness is read in exactly one readiness place (validate.ts:130) and precedes realization and authority (validate.ts:131-137); observable proof of the ordering is that W3 at its authored consent-required authority now returns needs-info/stale rather than needs-consent. No bypass exists: commit is gated by validation() (session.ts:67-68) and project.ts:101 reports ready only from an accepted commit; executeVirtual is still a stub. RESIDUAL GAPS (recorded, not blocking): (1) no gate pins the freshness-before-authority ORDERING - a one-line assertion that fixture W3 (consent-required) returns needs-info with a /stale/ reason would lock COUNCIL's requirement down; (2) the gate would also pass if freshness were implemented as a compile-path blocker in unresolvedFor, so it pins behaviour but not the architectural placement inside the one READY law; (3) spec.json still declares D1-016 surface as src/world.ts + worlds/, while the implementation now lives in validate.ts (D1-005's file) - a provenance/surface mismatch worth reconciling. Freshness verdict state 'needs-info' is a reasonable, internally consistent label here: contract.ts:121 has no 'stale' verdict, and the compile path already mapped its 'stale' unresolved reason to needs-info, so the two paths agree.

review.head: 7a96038951c2
review.note: ACCEPT (adversarial, mutation-tested; no --reject). SCOPE: bc39ae1 adds one gate() block, +21/-0 lines, 0 deletions (own gate, nothing widened); machine diff of every gate id+name in the whole gates dir vs bc39ae1~1 shows exactly one ADDITION and zero renames/removals. 79c204d touches compile.ts only (+46/-1). RED-BEFORE-FIX confirmed. MUTATION (disposable worktree, all three fire): (a) revert compile.ts to bc39ae1 -> D1-017 FAILS at 'Expected: not ready'; (b) unheldLink forced to return null -> FAILS; (c) add 'on' to CHAIN_PREPS -> control 'send note on Monday to work claude' FAILS (got needs-info, expected ready). ratchet verify D1-017 green; status --probe REGRESSED 0, 46/86 (45/85 -> 46/86, +1 gate +1 pass, nothing else moved); ratchet check exit 0, 5 pre-existing PROMOTE_PENDING warnings on unrelated tasks. PROBES (W4, authority prompt.send@1=allowed unless noted): 'send hello to Gemini via work claude', "send 'x' to Gemini via work claude", 'send hello to work claude and to Gemini', 'send hello to Gemini, then to work claude', 'send hello to work claude via Gemini', 'send hello to Gemini or to work claude' -> all needs-info, account=null, unresolved account:unknown (Gemini no longer absorbed). Controls intact: 'send hello to work claude' ready/claude-work; "send 'x' to work claude" ready; W1 'send hello' ready; W2 'send hello to claude' needs-choice/ambiguous; W2 'Ask Claude to explain this error: build failed' needs-choice/ambiguous; "send 'tell it to Gemini' to work claude" ready with prompt verbatim 'tell it to Gemini'; 'send note on Monday to work claude' ready/claude-work. No false positives introduced; fail-safe only tightens. Bonus: fix also stops Gemini leaking into the prompt body (pre-fix prompt was 'hello to Gemini'). RESIDUAL (pre-existing, NOT introduced, NOT worsened - byte-identical pre- and post-fix, so accepted as a new task not a rejection): preposition ellipsis still drops the unheld target - 'send hello to Gemini and work claude', 'send hello to Gemini, work claude', 'send hello to Gemini or work claude', 'send hello to work claude and Gemini', 'tell Gemini the report to work claude' all still READY on account:claude-work. Root cause compile.ts:538 - routeChain breaks at a word run not opened by a CHAIN_PREP, so a connector-joined clause with an omitted preposition is never examined. The gate name is absolute while the implementation is scoped to preposition-opened chains; the code comment at compile.ts:526 is honest about the narrower scope. Minor/inert: on blocked inputs the connector text stays in the prompt ('hello to Gemini, then'), harmless because the command cannot execute.

interpretation.ratchetModeGreen: the ratchet-mode gate suite (`bun run d1:gates`) exits green while open gates run as expected failures — it means open gaps are represented honestly and promoted gates have not regressed, NOT that the deliverable works

limitations: Gate results are claims about the code at the probed HEAD only.
A PROVEN task has promoted green gates but no independent review yet.
Fixture and simulated results are never live results.

Reviewer identity (`--by <label>`) is an auditable coordination label, not cryptographic proof that two labels are independent underlying actors; the engine enforces label separation, not actor independence (C2).
Ratchet-mode green (`d1:gates`) is not completion; only the probe-green frontier plus independent reviews, and finally the completion record, are (C4).
